title: Settlement Agreements: Account Status, Waiting Period, Cooling-Off and Offer-Count Conditions for an Offer
content:
# Settlement Agreements — When a Programme May Be Offered on an Account

The conditions below decide whether a programme of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements may be offered on a placed account at all. Each is tested on Ridgeline's own records for the placed account the offer would settle, as they stand before the offer is extended.

## 1. Account status

A settlement offer is extended only on a placed account whose status is validation period, active, arranged or hardship hold; accounts in placed, dispute hold or any terminal status receive no offer.

| Account status on the placed account | Offer |
|---|---|
| validation period, active, arranged, hardship hold | may be considered |
| placed (not yet worked), dispute hold, or any terminal status | no offer |

## 2. Waiting period after placement

A programme is offered only when the handling date is on or after the programme's waiting period counted from the account's placement date. The waiting period is the programme's waiting period figure in calendar days, the day after the placement date being day one. The clock starts from the placement date the placed account shows; the comparison is "not earlier than", and the handling date that is the last day of the waiting period satisfies it.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, 30-day waiting period):* on the 30th calendar day after the placement date the programme may be offered; on the 29th it may not. A programme whose waiting period is 0 may be offered from the placement date itself.

## 3. Cooling-off after an expired or defaulted settlement

A programme is not offered again on an account when the handling date is not later than the cooling-off period counted from the closing date of the account's most recent settlement that expired or defaulted. The cooling-off period is the re-offer cooling-off figure of the programme now to be offered, in calendar days, the day after that closing date being day one. The comparison is "later than": the last day of the cooling-off period itself still bars the programme.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, 15-day cooling-off period):* on the 15th calendar day after the closing date the programme is not offered; on the 16th it may be. The anchor is the most recent expired or defaulted settlement on that same account; a settlement that was withdrawn or fulfilled starts no cooling-off clock under this clause.

## 4. Offers in the last 12 months

When the count of settlement offers on the account in the last 12 months has reached a programme's offer limit, that programme is not offered. The count takes every settlement on the same placed account by its offer date, every programme and every status included, over the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date, both ends included.

*Hypothetical case:* the 365-day window runs from the 364th calendar day before the handling date through the handling date itself, so an account with offers dated 364 days and 20 days before the handling date counts two offers, while an offer dated 365 days before falls outside the window.

## Combined reading

Each clause is a condition of its own: a programme is offered on an account only where the status clause, its waiting period, its cooling-off period and its offer limit all allow it.
